Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Progressive failover banding — RTO/RPO options for GreenField

Marissa / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. As we discussed in the call this morning, GreenField is preparing to expand Redwood-backed inference into our fraud-detection and realtime-authorization pipelines. Our internal auditors and regulators require clearer commitments for cross-region failover and an explicit mapping of RTO/RPO by region and by service tier.

High-level asks:
- Primary (US-East): RTO <= 5 minutes, RPO = 0 (continuous replication)
- Secondary (EU) within same legal boundary: RTO <= 30 minutes, RPO <= 1 hour
- Cross-jurisdiction (APAC warm standby): RTO <= 4 hours, RPO <= 6 hours

We understand the cost and technical implications; we want a proposed amendment or exception we can present to our compliance and procurement teams that balances reliability with reasonable unit economics. Please include measurable acceptance criteria (how uptime and failovers will be measured), SLA credits/penalties, and any carveouts (maintenance, force majeure). Also include an estimated delta to our monthly committed bill.

Attaching our internal SRE playbook (referenced) and a short list of production domains we plan to move (will share separately).

Can you come back with a banded proposal and an initial cost delta by EOD Tuesday? We may also loop in our legal contact Samantha Lee for the final wording.

Thanks,
Alex Moretti
Head of Cloud Operations
GreenField Bank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Progressive failover banding — RTO/RPO options for GreenField

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Internal team looped in. High-level response below; I attached a draft amendment and a preliminary cost delta.

Proposal (service banding):
- Gold (Primary region; low latency-critical): RTO <= 5 min, RPO = 0 (synchronous or continuous replication where supported), target availability 99.99%
- Silver (Regional fallback within same legal boundary): RTO <= 30 min, RPO <= 1 hour, target availability 99.95%
- Bronze (Cross-jurisdiction warm standby): RTO <= 4 hours, RPO <= 6 hours, target availability 99.9%

Tradeoffs and notes:
- Gold requires reserved warm capacity and prioritized pre-warmed KV cache — material monthly premium.
- Silver can be achieved with cross-region async replication + periodic priming; cheaper but higher RPO.
- Bronze relies on warm-standby snapshots and slower cache rebuild; lower cost but higher recovery time and potential user-visible latency during cutover.
- Some model classes (large multimodal checkpoints) have longer cold-start latency and may require explicit pre-warm commitments in Gold.

Draft contract items included: measurement windows (1-minute resolution for failover events), SLO measurement methodology, and operational runbook pointer. I've attached SLA_amendment_draft.docx and cost_estimate_GreenField.csv for your review.

Next steps: please confirm which production domains you want Gold vs Silver vs Bronze. If you agree with the approach, we'll push a redline (Jonas) and route to DocuSign once legal approves. We can also schedule a short technical deep-dive (30 min) to walk SRE through priming/replication specifics.

Deliverables target: updated redline + final cost delta by EOD Monday (US) — can that work?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Progressive failover banding — technical feasibility notes

Marissa / Alex / team — quick technical notes from infra/SRE perspective:

- Continuous replication (RPO = 0) is feasible for request/response metadata and small KV state with our streaming replication; for very large model state and ephemeral per-session caches we rely on async KV snapshotting — so "RPO=0" must be scoped to the set of critical artifacts (auth tokens, small model params, feature vectors), not necessarily every in-memory cache. We'll include a scoping appendix.

- RTOs are dominated by two factors: model binary availability in the target region and the KV cache warm-up. For Gold-level <5m we need:
  * pre-deployed containers and reserved GPU capacity dedicated to your tenant (warm pool),
  * pre-populated KV cache or deterministic cache-warming hooks,
  * network routing pre-configured for automatic DNS failover or LB routing.

- Silver (<=30m) is realistic with async replication + scheduled cache priming; expect transient increased token latency for first 10–30 minutes post-cutover for some models.

- Bronze relies on snapshot restore and container spin-up; typical cold-start tails may push beyond 4 hours for very large multimodal models unless we reserve at least lightweight inference workers ahead of time.

Operational controls we recommend adding to the amendment:
- A definitive list of services/endpoints in each band,
- A documented failover playbook (who initiates, validation checks, and rollback criteria),
- A limit on SLA credits tied to mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-activate measurement windows.

I'll attach a short technical appendix draft to the Jira ticket ENG-2567. If GreenField wants Gold on high-throughput endpoints, we should prepare a capacity and cost snapshot.

—Kimberly
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: infra_appendix_GreenField.md (MD)]

Subject: Re: Progressive failover banding — proposed contract language

Alex / Marissa — following up with suggested amendment language for the SLA section. Below is a short sample clause you can use as a starting point; I'll add redline comments in the attached PDF: 

"Regional Failover and Recovery Banding. Redwood shall provide regional failover services according to the Service Band elected by Customer (Gold, Silver, Bronze). Each band specifies target Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) thresholds as set forth in Exhibit A. Customer acknowledges that RTO and RPO measurements are subject to the operational scope described in Exhibit B (technical scoping). Redwood's obligations are subject to (i) Customer provisioning of accurate list of critical endpoints and domains, (ii) Customer's timely completion of DNS and network configuration changes required for automated failover, and (iii) limitations set forth in the Force Majeure and Maintenance sections.

Measurement and Credits: Failover events will be measured using Redwood's monitoring pipeline (1-minute buckets) and verified within 72 hours. Service Credits for missed RTO commitments will be applied per Exhibit C and are capped at a monthly maximum equal to X% of the monthly fee for the impacted services.

Exceptions: Scheduled maintenance windows (>=48 hours notice), customer-triggered configuration changes, and third-party cloud provider outages shall be excluded from RTO/RPO calculations.

"

I suggest we include a 30-day pilot window where GreenField can validate the Gold behavior for one critical endpoint; if pilot metrics match expectations, the banding goes live for the agreed production domains. Deal reference: GF-2028-112.

DocuSign link for later: https://app.docusign.com/ABC12345

—Jonas
Director, Legal & Contracts, Redwood Inference
